expectations.text: Flags that transfer()'s fromAccount and toAccount are both plain strings and can be swapped silently
expectations.evidence: "`transfer(from, to)` — Swappable IDs (C1)... Call `transfer(destinationId, sourceId, amount)` — compiles, passes review, sends money backwards... Both values are strings."

expectations.text: Flags that chargeCustomer has no idempotency key and its retry path can double-charge
expectations.evidence: "`chargeCustomer()` — No idempotency key (M2)... Network blip on first call, retry fires, both succeed. Customer charged twice."

expectations.text: Flags the catch block that returns null as swallowing the error
expectations.evidence: "`chargeCustomer()` — Swallowed error returns null (X1)... Charge fails, function returns `null`, caller doesn't check, order marked paid anyway."

expectations.text: Flags money being held as a JS number (float) rather than integer minor units
expectations.evidence: No mention of float/number representation of money or minor units; `applyDiscount` is only noted as 'swappable numbers... local math helper, low blast'

expectations.text: Flags the interpolated raw SQL in purgeCanceledAccounts
expectations.evidence: Finding 4 covers only the dangerous `olderThan` default ('Default deletes everything'); no mention of raw SQL interpolation or injection

expectations.text: Flags the non-exhaustive switch over subscription status
expectations.evidence: "`updateSubscription()` — Non-exhaustive switch (F1)... Switch silently falls through."

expectations.text: Flags JSON.parse of the webhook body as unvalidated external input
expectations.evidence: "`handleWebhook()` — Unvalidated JSON (C7)... `JSON.parse` throws or fields are missing. Also: no signature verification."

expectations.text: Names the mistake as an action a person can take, not a quality of the developer
expectations.evidence: Every finding's 'Mistake' line is an action, e.g. "Call `purgeCanceledAccounts()` with no argument" and "Someone adds `"past_due"`... status"

expectations.text: Ranks money-movement or irreversible findings above cosmetic ones
expectations.evidence: Money/irreversible findings lead ('Blast: money loss', 'data loss'); cosmetic items pushed to 'Set aside (3)' and verdict names the two incident-grade ones

expectations.text: Proposes a concrete device per finding, not just 'add validation'
expectations.evidence: Each has a Device, e.g. "Atomic update with condition: `UPDATE ... SET balance = balance - $1 WHERE balance >= $1 RETURNING *`" and branded types / db.$transaction code
